sources.section: If you get lost or hurt; call for help

outcomes.scope: Lay activation order and location-first communication; no universal care sequence substituted for dispatcher or clinician guidance.
outcomes.owner: Emergency dispatch and search and rescue (H09, H11, H18)

card_changes.before: Z11-P63 | Prepare a concise structured rescue report before placing an emergency call |
card_changes.after: Z11-P63 | Call at once with your location first and keep a structured rescue report ready |

card_changes.before: objective: Deliver vital location, medical and hazard information cleanly in the first 30 seconds before a weak call drops.
card_changes.after: objective: Get help moving immediately and give dispatch your location first; a report prepared in advance fills in the rest without delaying the call.

card_changes.before: applies: Calling 911, texting 911 or composing a short satellite SOS message during any outdoor or disaster emergency.
card_changes.after: applies: Calling or texting 911 or sending a satellite SOS during any outdoor or disaster emergency; the report card is filled in before the trip and completed while help is on the way.

card_changes.before: equipment: Written pencil/paper notes or pre-typed message draft, phone/communicator and map.
card_changes.after: equipment: Phone or satellite communicator, map, and a report card or pre-typed message draft prepared before the trip.

card_changes.before: action: Write down six essentials BEFORE dialing or pressing send: (1) exact location or Last Known Point + coordinate format, (2) nature of emergency & number of injured/total people, (3) immediate medical red flags (responsiveness, breathing, bleeding, hypothermia/heat). @T02,T06,N09
card_changes.after: action: For unresponsiveness, abnormal breathing, severe bleeding or any doubt, call, text or press SOS now; do not stop to write notes first. With a phone, keep giving care while you talk to the dispatcher and follow the dispatcher's instructions. @T17,T02

card_changes.before: action: Add (4) surrounding access hazards (flooded roads, steep cliffs, ice, downed wires, weather), (5) shelter/water/battery status and clothing colors, and (6) confirmation whether you are staying put and your callback number. @T06,T02,N09
card_changes.after: action: Lead with LOCATION FIRST when speaking or texting (place name, trail or road, coordinates with their format, or your last known point) so that if the call drops, dispatch still knows where to send help. @T06,T02,N09

card_changes.before: action: Lead with LOCATION FIRST when speaking or texting on a fading battery or weak signal—if the call drops ten seconds in, dispatch still knows where to send help. @T06,T02,T11
card_changes.after: action: Keep a six-item report ready as an aid, not a precondition: (1) location format and last known point, (2) people and injuries, (3) red flags (responsiveness, breathing, bleeding, cold or heat), (4) access hazards, (5) shelter, water and battery, (6) stay-put plan and callback number. Fill it in before the trip and complete it while help is on the way or when the dispatcher asks. @T06,T11,N09

card_changes.before: failure: Spending two minutes explaining how the trip started on a 3% battery before ever stating the park name, trailhead or injury. @T06,T02
card_changes.after: failure: Delaying the call to write out a checklist while a companion is unresponsive or bleeding, or spending two minutes on how the trip started before stating the park name, trailhead or injury. @T17,T06,T02

card_changes.before: verify: Review your six written items aloud calmly before dialing and ask the dispatcher to confirm they received your exact location. @T06,T02,ED
card_changes.after: verify: Confirm the dispatcher has your location and callback number, then add the remaining report items as you learn them or as the dispatcher asks. @T06,T02,ED

card_changes.before: diagram: 1. Location & format FIRST | 2. People, injuries & hazards | 3. Stay-put plan & battery
card_changes.after: diagram: Life threat: call now, location first | Report card: six items prepared ahead | Add details while help is on the way

card_changes.before: visual: Exploded six-item dispatch-handoff card ordering location first, medical red flags, site hazards and stay-put confirmation for weak-signal calls. Conceptual, not to scale.
card_changes.after: visual: Call-first sequence: an immediate call that leads with location for any life threat, beside a six-item report card prepared before the trip and completed while help is on the way. Conceptual, not to scale.

card_changes.before: action: For chemical skin exposure, keep yourself clear of contamination, start decontamination as directed by the product label and Poison Control, and remove contaminated clothing if safe. card_changes.after: action: For chemical skin exposure, keep yourself clear of contamination, start decontamination as directed by the product label, Safety Data Sheet or Poison Control, and remove contaminated clothing if safe. For many liquid splashes, start rinsing promptly with running water unless that guidance says otherwise. Identify dry or water-reactive material to dispatch rather than improvising its treatment. @M32,M15,M16

outcomes.what: Infant formula removed from the generic safe-water list and given its own action (ready-to-feed safest; powder not sterile; chemical advisory needs bottled water or ready-to-feed) with a (see Z14-P74) link; W2C plate draws formula in its own panel.

sources.section: Ready-to-feed preference; Important: powder is not sterile
Extra precautions for some infants; Preparing formula during emergencies

outcomes.scope: Boundary and routing only; the high-risk preparation steps are left to the CDC page and the clinician. The link works in the full offline edition; a single-zone package labels it (full edition).

card_changes.before: objective: Apply safe-water standards consistently to teeth brushing, food washing, wound rinsing and infant feeding during advisories.
card_changes.after: objective: Apply safe-water standards consistently to teeth brushing, food washing and wound rinsing during advisories, and keep infant formula under its own preparation rules.

card_changes.before: equipment: Verified potable water, separate labeled utility water if permitted by notice, soap or alcohol hand sanitizer and clean utensils.
card_changes.after: equipment: Verified potable water, labeled utility water if the notice permits, ready-to-feed formula for formula-fed infants, soap and clean utensils.

card_changes.before: action: Use only bottled or properly boiled-and-cooled water for drinking, mixing infant formula, brushing teeth, washing ready-to-eat produce, making ice and washing food-contact dishes. @W29,W07
card_changes.after:
action: Use only bottled or properly boiled-and-cooled water for drinking, brushing teeth, washing ready-to-eat produce, making ice and washing food-contact dishes. @W29,W07
action: Treat infant formula as its own task (see Z14-P74): ready-to-feed is safest, especially under 2 months, premature or with a weakened immune system. Powder is not sterile, so safe water alone is not enough; follow current CDC and local directions. Under a chemical advisory, boiling does not help: use bottled water or ready-to-feed. @P26,P36,W07

card_changes.before: failure: Boiling water for drinking while brushing teeth, washing lettuce or mixing baby formula with unboiled advisory tap water. @W29,W07
card_changes.after: failure: Brushing teeth or washing lettuce with unboiled advisory tap water, or treating safe water as the only precaution when mixing powder for a newborn. @W29,W07,P26

card_changes.before: verify: Confirm every ingestion, oral-hygiene, food-prep, infant-formula and wound-care task draws exclusively from the verified potable supply. @W29,W07,ED
card_changes.after: verify: Confirm every ingestion, oral-hygiene, food-prep and wound-care task draws from the verified potable supply, and that infant formula follows its separate CDC directions. @W29,W07,P26,ED

card_changes.before: stop: If safe water cannot be secured for infant formula or wound care, prioritize ready-to-feed liquid formula and request immediate public-health or medical assistance. @W29,T02,ED
card_changes.after: stop: If safe water cannot be secured for infant formula or wound care, prioritize ready-to-feed liquid formula and request immediate public-health or medical assistance. @P26,W29,T02,ED

card_changes.after: diagram: Drinking, teeth, food & ice: potable water | Infant formula: separate rules; ready-to-feed safest | Do-Not-Use: zero tap contact

card_changes.after: visual: Task routing: drinking, teeth, food and dish tasks use verified potable water; infant formula follows its own CDC rules; wounds get potable water or saline; a Do Not Use notice stops all tap contact. Conceptual, not to scale.
